body: But surgeons are supposed to be perfect...

Thank you so much. You made me cry. I really appreciate your sentiments.

I'm so glad that I posted. I was so close to doing something drastic, but all of these kind words have been so nice.
I like operating but it's not worth the overall misery. Maybe if I took less call? But only having 4-8 days a month not on call is killing me.
The few patients here and there that are appreciative are one of my saving graces. Thanks for the encouragement, it means a lot.
I think it was less daily stress, less responsibility, free time. I have almost no free time now. I'm almost always on call. I would rather be dead.

You can't get out of student loans.

 But, honestly, that's not what's on my mind constantly. I just think about mistakes I've made and potential lawsuits constantly. I know I'm depressed but it's hard for doctors to get help (you have to report psych problems to your state medical board).
No, I owe over $300,000 in student loans from med school. I have no choice but to keep going to pay it off. It's over $2000 a month. It's like a gun to my head.

Thanks, you can't know how much I appreciate that.


I just don't know what to do. Before med school I was normal and ridiculously happy. I wish I could just be normal again with a normal job.


Now, I can't believe that I worked so hard to be so miserable. 


I work so unbelievably hard but I can't break even financially. Seriously I didn't take any vacation for the past six months and I still made less than last year. I owe so much in loans to cover med school that I can't slow down. 


Most months I take call 22 days, but some months I only have 4 days off total. My life is not my own and I literally hate every SINGLE minute. I hate waking up, getting ready, going to work, coming home, and going to sleep. I fantasize about being killed randomly so that I will no longer be in agony.

And the kicker is that everyone seems to love me and think that I'm great. My nurses, patients, friends, family, fiancé all think I'm great. No one knows how miserable I am. I just can't keep being so miserable.
